payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.interpretation: common or complementary evidence
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: While both demonstrate strong effect modification, feature 166 shows additional robust signals for treatment prediction and outcome prognosis, suggesting a role as both a confounder and effect modifier, whereas 165 is primarily an effect modifier.
themes.interpretation: Lung lobe-specific mass findings are strong candidates for effect modification, with variable evidence for confounding.
themes.name: Lung Mass Localization

themes.disagreements: High consistency across candidates; both features demonstrate strong evidence for being both confounders and effect modifiers.
themes.interpretation: Quantitative PET metrics (SUVmax and cerebellar FDG uptake) consistently appear as both confounders and effect modifiers.
themes.name: PET Quantitative Metrics

themes.disagreements: Significant disparity in signal strength: inhaler dosage (170) is a robust confounder and effect modifier, illicit drug use (162) is primarily a confounder, and hypothyroidism (161) provides only weak, non-robust evidence.
themes.interpretation: Baseline health indicators and medication usage show varying degrees of importance, ranging from strong dual roles to negligible evidence.
themes.name: Baseline Health and Medication

themes.disagreements: Candidates exhibit divergent roles: feature 163 suggests a role as an effect modifier (via R-learner), while feature 167 suggests a role as a confounder (via predictive forest outcome).
themes.interpretation: The mere presence of imaging procedures (CT, MRI) provides weak and inconsistent evidence for either confounding or effect modification.
themes.name: Imaging Procedural Evidence

themes.disagreements: None; this is a single-candidate theme with moderate evidence across multiple roles.
themes.interpretation: The type of prior immunotherapy shows moderate evidence of acting as both a confounder and an effect modifier.
themes.name: Immunotherapy Specification

themes.disagreements: Features 171 and 172 are purely prognostic with no treatment or effect signals, whereas 173 demonstrates clear treatment prediction and effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Imaging findings of orbital or cranial abnormalities showing varying levels of prognostic and causal importance.
themes.name: Orbital and Cranial Imaging Findings

themes.disagreements: Ki67 shows the strongest univariable effect signal, while KEAP1 and KRAS VAF rely more on forest-based methods for effect evidence.
themes.interpretation: Molecular and proliferative biomarkers showing consistent signals for effect modification and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Molecular and Pathological Biomarkers

themes.disagreements: Knee osteoarthritis is a dominant confounder; drug allergies are essentially noise; JVD and LDH show moderate multifaceted signals.
themes.interpretation: General clinical and laboratory assessments with divergent roles ranging from strong confounding to no evidence.
themes.name: General Clinical and Laboratory Findings

themes.disagreements: Lesion size (183) demonstrates strong evidence for outcome prognosis and treatment heterogeneity, whereas lesion presence (182) lacks a meaningful prognostic signal and exhibits only weak effect modification support.
themes.interpretation: Measurements focusing on the presence and magnitude of lesions, both of which show strong signals as predictors of treatment assignment.
themes.name: Lesion Attributes

themes.disagreements: While all three are strong treatment predictors, the evidence for effect modification varies, with line of therapy (184) showing more consistent support across families than lisinopril dose (186).
themes.interpretation: Systemic therapy markers, including line of therapy and specific medication use (lipids and lisinopril), which strongly predict treatment and often correlate with outcomes.
themes.name: Medical Therapy

themes.disagreements: Liver metastasis (188) is a strong candidate for both confounding and effect modification, while general liver function (187) shows only negligible, inconsistent signals.
themes.interpretation: Assessments of liver health, ranging from qualitative function to the presence of metastatic disease.
themes.name: Liver Status

themes.disagreements: Lobectomy type (190) shows moderate signals for treatment and outcome prediction, whereas leptomeningeal enhancement (181) is purely prognostic and an effect modifier with no treatment prediction signal.
themes.interpretation: Anatomical or procedural details from imaging (leptomeninges) and surgery (lobectomy type) that show significant signals for treatment heterogeneity.
themes.name: Surgical & Imaging Specifics

themes.disagreements: Strong evidence for confounding, but evidence for effect modification is weak (R-learner 5/15).
themes.interpretation: Patient living arrangements, which serve as strong predictors for both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Social Context

themes.disagreements: Lung disease diagnosis exhibits strong treatment prediction and effect modification, whereas lung auscultation findings are primarily prognostic with minimal treatment association.
themes.interpretation: Pulmonary statuses characterized by clinical diagnosis and physical examination findings that strongly influence outcome prognosis.
themes.name: Pulmonary Comorbidity and Symptomatology

themes.disagreements: SUVmax and histology show moderate stability in effect modification signals, whereas cancer stage and mass morphology show negligible or inconsistent support.
themes.interpretation: Intrinsic tumor characteristics derived from imaging and pathology that may modify treatment response.
themes.name: Tumor Morphological and Metabolic Characteristics

themes.disagreements: Lymph node dissection status provides a credible signal for effect modification, while metastasis count and lymphadenopathy status lack consistent support.
themes.interpretation: Measurements related to the surgical or radiographic assessment of lymphatic spread.
themes.name: Nodal Involvement Status

themes.disagreements: The surgical procedure of dissection (201) is a strong treatment predictor and effect modifier, whereas the pathological status (202) provides negligible signal across all roles.
themes.interpretation: Mediastinal assessment indicators, distinguishing between the act of dissection and the resulting nodal status.
themes.name: Mediastinal Assessment

themes.disagreements: Cisplatin (204) shows strong outcome prognosis and effect modification; gemcitabine (208) is primarily prognostic; G12C inhibitors (207) show only weak evidence of effect modification via R-learner.
themes.interpretation: Systemic chemotherapy agents with varying roles in outcome prognosis and treatment effect heterogeneity.
themes.name: Systemic Chemotherapy

themes.disagreements: Lisinopril (209) is a clear confounder; calcium carbonate (203) acts as both a confounder and effect modifier; denosumab (205) is primarily an effect modifier; dexamethasone (206) and MET inhibitors (210) are weak or only prognostic.
themes.interpretation: Supportive, concurrent, or targeted medications exhibiting a range of confounding and effect-modifying signals.
themes.name: Supportive and Concurrent Medications

themes.disagreements: Morphine shows strong evidence across all roles, while oxycodone exhibits only weak prognostic signals and no significant treatment or effect modification evidence.
themes.interpretation: Opioid-based pain management markers
themes.name: Opioid Pain Management

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
